reason: The file is `bat`'s recorded highlighting output: every token is wrapped in ANSI colour escapes, so the bytes are a terminal transcript rather than a CSS source file. The tree-sitter grammar reports an error on the first escape byte, which is what makes it residue rather than a defect.

The file writes `@keyframes blink { 0%, 49% { ... } 50%, 100% { ... } }`, and tree-sitter-css 0.23's `keyframe_block` takes exactly one of `from`, `to`, or an `integer_value` before its block, with no comma-separated selector list. The grammar reports an ERROR over each list, so the oracle has no walk to compare against; a comma-separated keyframe selector is ordinary CSS that every browser accepts.

The file nests `@container (max-width: 224px) { ... }` inside a rule's block. tree-sitter-css 0.23 predates container queries and cannot read a bare `feature_query` as an `at_rule`'s only query in block position, so it reports an ERROR over `(max-width: 224px)` and the oracle has no walk to compare against.

The file writes `@source '../node_modules/fumadocs-ui/dist/**/*.js';`, a Tailwind 4 at-rule whose only argument is a string. tree-sitter-css 0.23 accepts neither a string as an `at_rule` query nor a `postcss_statement` in top-level position, so it reports an ERROR that runs from the terminating semicolon into the next rule and the oracle has no walk to compare against.
